DataSigma (customer): hitting 401 invalid_api_key for all requests since this morning. we haven't changed code, just redeployed. can you help?
Samir G: sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact Authorization header (redact most of the key but keep the first/last 4 chars)?
DataSigma (customer): `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_4f3a...9d2b` — we tried curl and our SDK, both 401.
Jess Torres: curious — is that exactly what you see in logs or did you copy from an internal doc? sometimes copy/paste introduces invisible chars.
DataSigma (customer): copied from a shared doc inside Confluence. i can run a hexdump if you want.
Samir G: please do a quick sanity check first: run `printf "%s" "<paste-key-here>" | xxd` and paste the output. that will show any odd bytes.
DataSigma (customer): output: ```
00000000: 536b 5f6c 6976 655f 3466 3361 e2 8f  Sk_live_4f3a....
00000010: 6563 2e2e 2e39 6432 62                   ec...9d2b
```
Rohit Patel: that 0xE2 0x8F in the middle is suspicious — it's a multi-byte sequence, not part of an ASCII API key. could be a Unicode control char.
Jess Torres: 0xE2 0x8F corresponds to U+202E (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE) when combined with following bytes — a bidi control. if inserted inside the key it'll change how it displays and how it's transmitted.
DataSigma (customer): whoa. i can see it in the hexdump but in the Confluence snippet it just looks normal (maybe renders reversed?). how would that get in there?
Samir G: some editors or copy tools (Word, rich text editors, maybe pasting from PDFs) can insert bidi marks. confluence's code block might hide them visually. also sneaky when someone does directional formatting.
Infra Bot: ticket created: #SUP-54721 (escalation) — please add logs and redacted key on the ticket.
Rohit Patel: short repro recomendation for you: run this python snippet to print codepoints and check for control chars: ````
python3 - <<'PY'
s = "<paste-key-here>"
print([hex(ord(c)) for c in s])
PY
````
DataSigma (customer): ran it, got: `['0x53','0x6b','0x5f','0x6c','0x69','0x76','0x65','0x5f','0x34','0x66','0x33','0x61','0x202e','0x65','0x63','0x2e','0x2e','0x2e','0x39','0x64','0x32','0x62']` — yep there's `0x202e`.
Samir G: ok that's the cause. the server expects the literal ASCII sequence; the control char makes the token mismatch and we return 401.
Jess Torres: mitigation steps for customer: 1) rotate the compromised key (we'll revoke the old one on our end if you want). 2) replace the stored key in Confluence/CI with the new one but *paste as plain text* or use our Vault integration. 3) run the codepoint check before pasting into deploys.
DataSigma (customer): can you revoke the old key? we rotated locally but maybe other copies exist.
Samir G: yes we can revoke. @Infra Bot create a rotate/revoke action and mark the old key as compromised. please provide the last 4 chars so we hit the right one.
DataSigma (customer): last 4 are `9d2b`.
Infra Bot: action logged: revoke request submitted for key ending `9d2b`. ticket #SUP-54721 updated.
Rohit Patel: long term, we should add a helpful error: if an API key contains non-ASCII or bidi control chars, return a different diagnostic code and include guidance in the message (but not the raw key). i'll file a proposal on eng-runtime.
Samir G: +1 — help customers faster. @Jess can you add a note in the support KB about bidi/control chars in keys and the python/xxd checks?
Jess Torres: on it. i'll also add a short Confluence note with the `printf | xxd` and python snippet and mention common paste sources (Word, PDFs, some copy/paste on macOS that preserves directionality).
DataSigma (customer): thanks team — rotated and redeployed, requests now return 200. you can close the ticket after revocation confirmed. :white_check_mark:
Infra Bot: key revocation confirmed by security: old key `...9d2b` revoked. ticket #SUP-54721 closed by Infra Bot.
Samir G: great! leaving a short postmortem in the ticket with root cause: U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE injected into stored key in Confluence. prevention: prefer secret store, add validation in our API, and KB article.
Jess Torres: adding KB link to the ticket and to this thread: https://redwood.example/kb/apikey-bidi-control-chars
DataSigma (customer): appreciated — that was a weird one. learned something new :) :raised_hands:
